#### Homogeneity 4: Identical and independent attachment 

In a [bipartite random network NPSEM](#def-bipartite-npsem-ie), each row of the adjacency matrix ${\Psi}_{si}$ (person $i$'s network weights) belongs to person $i$'s observational unit. Identical structural distributions then say that every row is generated by the same $1 \times q$ array of equations $F_{{\mathbf \Psi_s}}$, and single-world independence, with each row taken as a single variable (@def-brnffrcistg), says that the rows' one-step-ahead counterfactuals are mutually independent. Nothing is assumed about the error terms, and entries within a row need not be independent: a person's links to different places may share a disturbance. Each person in the model attaches to a selection of places independently of any other person and based on identical equations. This is not an extra assumption of the [BRNFFRCISTG](#def-brnffrcistg); it is what the model's assumptions say about the rows. 

Here each row may depend on the whole past, $\mathbf V_{s-1}$ and $\mathbf \Psi_{s-1}$. [Local row formation](#def-local-row-formation) restricts this further: a person's row depends on the past only through bounded summaries of their own history and network values and of their own past rows, for example the neighborhoods they visited the week before. That is what makes the row equation estimable from one realization ([Remark 7](#rem-rows)).

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Structural: Places } (\mathbb{R}) \\
&   R_{sj}                   & &= f_{ R_s}( U_{ R_{sj}},   g_{VR}(\mathbf{V}_{s-1}, {[\mathbf \Psi^T_s]}_{j}) ) \\
&   T_{sj}                   & &= f_{ T_s}( U_{ T_{sj}},  R_{sj})                                 \\
\text{Structural: People } (\mathbb{R}) \\
&   M_{si}                  & &=     f_{ M_s} ( U_{ M_{si}} ,  V_{s-1,i},    M_{s-1, i},  g_{TM}(\mathbf{T}_{s}, {\Psi}_{si}))       \\
&   V_{si}                  & &=     f_{ V_s}( U_{ V_{si}},  M_{si},  V_{s-1, i})                                                \\
\text{Structural: People in places } (\mathbb{R}^{1 \times q}) \\
&  {\Psi}_{si}   & &= F_{{\mathbf \Psi_s}}(\mathbf U_{{\Psi}_{si}}, \mathbf{V}_{s-1}, \mathbf{\Psi}_{s-1})  \\
\end{aligned}
$$




where ${[\mathbf \Psi^T_s]}_{j}$ is the $j^{th}$ row of the transpose of the adjacency matrix $\mathbf{\Psi}_{s}$.
